1. Description

This pairing examines the areal extent of sea ice on the Arctic Ocean. It specifically focuses on the average extent for September, which is frequently used as an indicator because it is typically the month when the ice reaches its annual minimum extent. September sea ice extent is one part of Figure 1 in EPA’s Arctic Sea Ice indicator. The technical documentation for that indicator provides additional information on the value of examining September trends.

Technically, this data set covers the entire zone from 30.98°N to 90°N latitude, so it includes all sea ice in the Northern Hemisphere. However, in summer and fall months like September, ice is highly unlikely to exist outside the Arctic region. Thus, this feature appropriately characterizes ice on the Arctic Ocean and its immediately adjacent water bodies (e.g., around Greenland and the islands of northern Canada).

This feature includes the following components:

  • Historical observations since 1979, which was the first year of comprehensive satellite data coverage.
  • Modeled projections from 2015 to 2100 for four climate scenarios.
  • A modeled hindcast from 1950 to 2014.
